TESTIMONY BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON AGRICULTURE, CONSERVATION AND FORESTRY
IN SUPPORT OF LD 398
An Act to Amend the Definition of "Transient Occupancy" in the Laws Governing the Maine Land Use Planning Commission
April 15, 2025

Senator Talbot Ross, Representative Pluecker, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry, my name is Ben Godsoe. I am the Planning Manager for
the Maine Land Use Planning Commission (Commission or LUPC), with'm the Department of
Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (DACF). I am speaking in support of LD 398, "An Act to
Amend the Definition of `Transient Occupancy' in the Laws Governing the Maine Land Use Planning Commission. "
LUPC serves as the planning, zoning, and land use permitting authority for the unorganized and
deorganized areas of the state, including all townships, most plantations, and certain small towns (unorganized territories or UT). These areas either have no local government or have chosen not
to administer land use controls at the local level. LUPC's service area includes more than 10.4
million acres, nearly half of the State's geographic area.
The Use Regulation law, Title 12, � 681 et seq., created the Commission and identified the
agency's mission. Currently, the statute provides that a permit is not required for a campsite in a
management subdistrict and includes a definition of "campsite." The definition reads in part:
" ...Campsite " means a camping location containing tents, registered recreational
vehicles, or similar devices usedfor camping... A campsite may be designed to contain a maximum of 4 camping sites for transient occupancy by 12 or fewer people per site...
I2 M.R.S. �682(15).
Transient occupancy is defined as . . " .occupancy that does not exceed 120 days in a calendar
year. "]2 MR. S. �682(15).
As written, the statute limits the camping season for exempt campsites to 120 days, which generally encompasses Memorial Day to Labor Day. Historically, that timeframe was the camping season for most residents and visitors to Maine. However, warmer weather extending

The proposed bill would extend occupancy for exempt campsites by 30 days. Expanding the definition of transient occupancy to 150 days would encompass Memorial Day to Indigenous
Peoples Day. LUPC does not anticipate that allowing one additional month for seasonal camping
would have a significant adverse impact on the natural character or existing resources in the UT.
Camping is a traditional recreational use in the LUPC's service area. Extending the camping
season to allow for camping into October would support fall hunting and fishing, which are also traditional uses in our service area. Because campsite occupancy would still be limited to a
reasonable timeframe, the LUPC supports extending the transient occupancy definition to
include 150 days.

Testimony ofRep. Timothy Guerrette on
LD 398, "An Act to Amend the Definition of "Transient Occupancy" in the
Laws Governing the Maine Land Use Planning Commission" Before the Joint Standing Committee on Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry
April 15, 2025
Good afternoon, Senator Talbot Ross, Representative Pluecker, and members of the
Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry Committee. I'm Rep. Tim Guerrette, representing
Caribou in Aroostook County, and I'm here to introduce LD 398, "An Act to Amend
the Definition of "Transient Occupancy" in the Laws Governing the Maine Land
Use Planning Commission."
This bill calls for extending the definition of transient occupancy from 120 to 150 days within the Maine Land Use Planning Commission's jurisdiction. As changing weather patterns continue to extend the viable outdoor season in Maine, allowing an additional 30 days for camping is both practical and timely. This update would give individuals and families greater opportunity to enjoy longer stays in Maine's natural areas while continuing to support rural economies and the values of outdoor living that are so central to our state.
I respectfully urge the committee to support this sensible change.
Thank you--I'm happy to answer any questions.
Timothy C. Guerrette
State Representative
